questions.question: Please define audience source/methodology. If you build proprietary audiences, please include sources and seeds.
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint builds proprietary audiences using a combination of first-party HCP data, de-identified medical and pharmacy claims, and real-time behavioral and contextual signals. PulsePoint's HCP data is built on Medscape first party data. We rely on Medscape CRM as the source because re-identification requires a consented foundation-- something only Medscape provides at scale. DTC audiences are derived from millions of annual claims and enriched with engagement and content consumption signals using our patented contextual engine mapped to National Library of Medicine's taxonomy. All data is HIPAA- and NAI-compliant and refreshed continuously to maintain accuracy.

questions.question: How do you ensure compliance with global data privacy regulations (e.g., GDPR, CCPA, LGPD) and state health data regulations
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint ensures compliance by using only de-identified data for DTC targeting and obtaining named, first-party consent for HCP data. We follow HIPAA, NAI, GDPR, CCPA, and LGPD guidelines, and apply Safe Harbor or Expert Determination methods to protect patient privacy. Data use is governed by strict contracts, population thresholds, and internal audits to meet both global and state-level health data requirements.
questions.note: GDPR/CCPA/state health-data compliance is the legal/privacy row. Library holds an answer; the skill says not to use it.

questions.question: What identity graphs are integrated with your platform? (LiveRamp, Axciom, etc.)
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint operates its own identity graph. We also are integrated with enternal partners such as LiveRamp/RampID and other privacy-compliant ID solutions, including UID2 and ID5.

questions.question: What levels of geographic targeting are available? (Zip11, Zip9, Zip5, Postal, H3, Household-Home Address, etc.)
questions.approved_answer: PulsePoint supports geographic targeting at ZIP levels, along with DMA, county, state, postal code and custom radius targeting. We also support household-level targeting based on our identity graph.

=== ./client-strategy/loopio-11344328.md
id: loopio-11344328
question: DTC audience methodology?
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:00:36+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

PulsePoint's DTC audience methodology combines medically mapped contextual data, online audience behaviors, clinical data, and signals from Internet Brands' owned and operated health sites, such as WebMD. This multi-source approach enables the identification of consumer audiences based on their medical interests, behaviors, conditions, and engagement with trusted health platforms. By integrating these diverse data points, PulsePoint delivers precise, relevant messaging to target audiences, enhancing the effectiveness of direct-to-consumer (DTC) campaigns.
 
 For DTC:
 - Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real time toward the prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
 -- Life science companies often utilize HCP data to inform DTC audience segmentation. 
 - Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
 - Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 - Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
 - Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
 - OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
 - Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand or PulsePoint
 - Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
 - IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
 We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.

=== ./client-strategy/loopio-11344753.md
id: loopio-11344753
question: What is the methodology behind your segment creation? (Ex. Use a seed audience that is then modeled out for distribution)
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:03:12+00:00
tags: 
source: loopio

PulsePoint leverages a first party data foundation at the core of our business. The HCP identity graph uses the power of Medscape's physician member database to authenticate 3.2 million NPI numbers across the United States to inform and validate all HCP targeting from platform. The offline NPI numbers are translated into online IDs within a proprietary identity infrastructure and through the use of 4x verified onboarders, and campaigns are then able to reach the physicians within their digital footprint. PulsePoint is specifically focused to developing a best-in-class, accurate translation of the NPI number to digital ID, which has generated an NPI graph that has an addressability rate of 90%+ on average (i.e. with 10k NPIs, PulsePoint can deliver to 9.5k of those within a 30-day window). 
 
 Customized consumer audiences are created using claims data signals such as ICD-10 codes, J-Codes, NDC Codes, and CPT codes to develop a seed that is further modeled out based on diagnosis and treatment propensity by age, gender and zip code. The models directly reference our HIPPA compliant database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims powered by a Forian data claims data API and are planned and activated according to NAI privacy guidelines. Additional consumer data signals that reference our proprietary HCP database in an anonymized way, such as likely patients of target HCPs, geographical relevance to practice locations of specific HCPs are also leveraged for modeling purposes. Each model is fully customized.

=== ./client-strategy/loopio-12865757.md
id: loopio-12865757
question: Do you use tokenization or third-party identity resolution?
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2025-08-13T19:52:25+00:00
tags: Legal Approved
source: loopio

Yes. PulsePoint uses both tokenization and third party identity resolution to securely match and activate audiences.
 
Tokenization replaces any personally identifiable information with pseudonymous  IDs.
 
For identity resolution, we work with approved third party partners to match first party and third party data across devices and channels. This process allows us to connect deterministic identifiers like NPIs or hashed HCP emails with probabilistic signals, enabling a unified, privacy-preserving  view of the audience.
 
Both processes are in alignment with legal and regulatory compliance.

########## rfi-2026/rfi2026-kso-024.md
id: rfi2026-kso-024
question: What channels/relationships are currently on the product roadmap?
stack: RFI 2026
updated: 2026-08-20T00:00:00+00:00
tags: Optimization & Reporting, Data, Partnerships, HCP
source: PulsePoint Submission 2027 KSO DSP Pharma RFI

Outside of the channels and relationships that are already organized into the PulsePoint activation ecosystem, there are various of initiatives that are on the roadmap. In 2026, PulsePoint is focused on ensuring that we have a comprehensive set of walled garden biddable media platforms that we are able to push our data to for activation. Meta, LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Google, Bing, Pinterest, and other social platforms that clients are bringing to us as priority are built into the platform, either in GA or in beta. PulsePoint is also working to ensure that the relationships that we have with data partners for data onboarding and verification, and healthcare-specific measurement partners such as Crossix and IQVIA, are built into our suite or reporting products. This will allow clients to select into seeing platform reporting in accordance to more general measurement contracts that brands work with. PulsePoint is focused on ensuring that the technology can constantly evolve towards more sophistication in HCP and patient reach, and ultimately enabling the platform to stitch those two audiences together for maximum brand cohesion in the market, resulting in the highest ROI possible for brands. This means that we are working through Adaptive Optimization elevation, measurement dashboards that clients can use to pull insights and discover near real-time insights on how the media delivery backs into claims behaviors, updating proprietary data segments based on deeper claims and digital brand signals. PulsePoint is always open to demoing all of our new offers and proprietary technology solutions to clients, and look forward to the opportunity to share our continuous updates.

########## rfi-2026/rfi2026-cmi2025-016.md

question: Please list all reporting capabilities. (Specific reporting capabilities to call out, in platform reporting view, downloadable reports. Include all reporting metrics available)
stack: RFI 2026
updated: 2025-01-01T00:00:00+00:00
tags: Supply, Optimization & Reporting, HCP, DTC
source: CMI Agency RFI - 2025

source: loopio

PulsePoint’s reporting capabilities provide a comprehensive and real-time view of campaign performance, enabling advertisers to track and optimize their efforts across various channels, devices, and audience segments. The reporting is designed to be highly granular, offering insights into impressions, engagement, conversions, audience behaviors, and health-related outcomes.
 
Key Reporting Features:
1) Real-Time Reporting Dashboards:
PulsePoint offers real-time dashboards that provide up-to-the-minute insights into campaign metrics such as impressions, clicks, click-through rates (CTR), and conversions. These dashboards allow for immediate adjustments to campaigns based on live data.
2) Audience Segmentation & Performance:
The reporting platform offers detailed insights into how specific audience segments perform, allowing advertisers to analyze engagement rates by segments such as de-identified consumers, healthcare professionals (HCPs), and condition-based targeting. Advertisers can also view performance by demographics (e.g., age, gender) and behaviors (e.g., content interactions).
3) Site-Level and Placement Insights:
Advertisers can see exactly where their ads were served, including details at the site, app, or page level. This helps understand the quality and context of inventory sources. In addition, placement data such as whether ads were above or below the fold can be tracked.
4) Cross-Channel and Device Reporting:
PulsePoint provides a cross-channel view, enabling advertisers to see how their campaigns are performing across display, video, connected TV (CTV), digital out-of-home (DOOH), and mobile. Device-level data (e.g., mobile, desktop, tablet, CTV) also ensures that campaigns can be optimized based on device performance.
5) Viewability and Brand Safety Metrics:
Integrated with verification partners such as DoubleVerify, the platform tracks viewability rates, fraud detection, and brand safety compliance. These metrics help ensure that campaigns are served in trusted environments and reach the intended audience.
6) Geographic and Demographic Reporting:
Advertisers can view campaign performance at a geographic level, from national to zip code, allowing for precise regional insights. Similarly, demographic data provides insights into how different groups within the target audience are interacting with the campaign.
7) Post-Engagement and Health Outcomes:
For healthcare campaigns, PulsePoint offers advanced insights into post-engagement behaviors, such as prescription lift or visits to health-related sites. Integrated data partnerships enable advertisers to measure actual health outcomes based on ad exposure.
 
Sample Metrics in Reports:
Impressions
Clicks and CTR
Viewability Rate
Conversions (e.g., form fills, downloads)
Audience Breakdown (by age, gender, conditions)
Geographic Reach (country, state, zip code)
Device Performance (mobile, desktop, CTV, etc.)
Ad Placement Data (above/below fold)
Frequency & Recency
 
PulsePoint’s reporting can also be customized based on specific KPIs and goals. Additionally, advertisers can use the API to export reports into external systems or BI tools for further analysis, ensuring seamless integration with your internal data workflows.

Our Smart Pixel builds audiences in real time from page views, site behavior and search activity, including URL-level mapping and keyword tracking. CMI-042.draft: Our roadmap focuses on three areas. First, we are expanding where clients can activate our healthcare data across walled-garden biddable platforms: Meta, LinkedIn, X, Reddit, Google, Bing and Pinterest are built into the platform in GA or beta, and we are adding the platforms clients rank as priorities. Second, we are building our data-onboarding and verification partners, and healthcare measurement partners such as Crossix and IQVIA, into our reporting suite, so you can view platform reporting in line with your brand's measurement contracts. Third, we are deepening HCP and patient reach and connecting the two audiences. That work includes Adaptive Optimization enhancements, measurement dashboards that show in near real time how media delivery ties to claims behavior, and proprietary segments refreshed with deeper claims and digital brand signals. ##### /mnt/memory/rfi-answer-library/client-strategy/loopio-11344430.md
id: loopio-11344430
question: Specifically - What offline measurement solutions does your platform offer?
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2024-10-14T20:00:42+00:00

PulsePoint offers a range of offline measurement solutions that integrate both clinical and consumer data, enabling comprehensive analysis of campaign effectiveness, particularly for healthcare marketing. Key offline measurement solutions include:
 1. Claims-Based Measurement: PulsePoint partners with Forian to provide claims-based insights. This includes tracking prescription lift and diagnosing behavior changes directly related to campaigns, using data from over 220 million patients, 3 billion annual pharmacy claims, and 2 billion annual medical claims. This allows brands to measure the real-world impact of their digital campaigns on patient behavior and health outcomes.
 2. Test & Control Groups: PulsePoint enables the creation of test and control groups for campaign effectiveness studies. This approach helps determine the incremental impact of advertising by comparing groups exposed to ads versus those who aren't, measuring actual clinical outcomes like prescriptions filled or treatments received.
 3. Komodo Health Integration: PulsePoint integrates with Komodo Health to provide more granular offline measurements, including reach into specific audiences and deeper insights into clinical outcomes, helping to track long-term behavior shifts post-campaign.
 4. In-Geo Performance Tracking: PulsePoint provides geographic-level analysis, particularly when campaigns are tied to specific healthcare facilities or regions. This enables offline measurement by analyzing behaviors like clinic visits or prescription fills in targeted areas.
 5. Linear / CTV Overlap: PulsePoint works with Comscore to understand the overlap and impact of running both offline linear TV buys in conjunction with digital advertising.
 These solutions are designed to provide actionable insights into real-world health outcomes and the tangible effects of marketing efforts on treatment patterns, all while maintaining HIPAA compliance.

LIFE users are able to use any desired buy types within the platform, depending on the goal of the tactic and the inventory selection. Open Exchange (OE): Preferred, no floor, competitive pricing. Full OE access via 40+ integrated SSPs across all formats. Private Marketplace (PMP): Preferred, variable floor by publisher, no platform minimum. question: List integrations with third party brand safety providers and any proprietary brand safety offerings. Describe, at a high level, what makes brand safety in your platform differentiated or unique.
stack: Client Strategy
updated: 2025-04-11T14:39:44+00:00
tags: Legal Approved
source: loopio

PulsePoint partners with industry-leading organizations including DoubleVerify to combat fraud and invalid traffic. WIthin the UI, PulsePoint encourages the use of off-the-shelf DV pre-bid solutions that prevent all campaigns from considering any ad that may qualify as suspicious traffic/fraud. We also support Authentic Brand Safety to ensure brand safety settings are updated in real-time. In addition to combating fraud and any testing that may be identified and blocked from auction, PulsePoint partners with advanced fraud solution and uses fraud lookalike signals to invalidate any potential suspicious impression that may have passed through the initial pre-bid scan. All invalidated impressions and associated actions are scrubbed from the UI so that they are never counted in platform delivery and spend. PulsePoint also automatically applies a daily supply scrubbing for MFA content through Jounce, and pre-vetted bundles of brand safe supply through Curated Markets.

CMI-041.draft: Every campaign runs with DoubleVerify brand safety and IVT protection by default, and users customize DV settings for each targeting tactic. That includes DV Authentic Brand Safety (ABS), which updates settings in real time; IAS Quality Sync is available in the platform as the equivalent. To prevent fraud and invalid traffic, we work with DoubleVerify, Pixalate and HUMAN. Fraud lookalike signals also invalidate suspicious impressions that get past the pre-bid scan. Jounce Media scrubs supply daily for made-for-advertising (MFA) content, and Curated Markets offer pre-vetted bundles of brand-safe supply.

stack: Client Strategy- Cleaned
updated: 2025-10-07T18:14:12+00:00
tags: Data; DTC; HCP; Optimization & Reporting
source: loopio

We have several different targeting capabilities for both HCP and DTC readily available directly in platform.
 
 For HCP:
 - HCP Direct Match for NPI, Specialty, Clinical Behavior, and Practice. For NPI, we have deterministic 1:1 NPI targeting, backed up by a database of over 3.2 million HCPs in the US, and with NPI level reporting. For specialty, target and activate your HCP audience based on their primary/secondary specialties and professions. For clinical behavior, target HCPs based on their clinical behavior e.g. prescriptions, diagnoses, procedures etc (Rx, Dx, Px). For practice, target HCPs and HCP decision-makers at their practice and point-of-care facilities.
 
 For DTC:
 - Bespoke Audiences: Clinical signals for DTC are the results of the production of audience models that are optimized in real-time toward the prevalence of diagnosis and treatment by age, gender, and zip code at delivery. Custom claims-based models based on a database of 220MM+ Patients and 3BB annual pharmacy claims. Audience models created follow NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions.
 -- Life science companies often utilize HCP data to inform DTC audience segmentation. 
 - Health Pages: Capture the consumer & patient’s attention at the exact moment intent is signaled. Target audiences consuming relevant health content.
 - Health Populations: Target audiences who have recently engaged with content for specific health conditions and treatments. Populations are built dynamically using the entire browsing profile of the individual, which allows you to capture the user regardless of the page they are on or arriving from.
 - Health Populations+: This takes our foundational Health Populations Audiences and includes their first-party signals through PulsePoint’s proprietary access to endemic website data.
 - Rx Populations: Rx Populations reaches qualified, scalable DTC audiences without sacrificing performance by combining PulsePoint’s contextually created audiences (HealthPop) with RX data to maintain quality and scale, while having a positive impact on AQ during later stage moments of the health journey.
 - OTC Populations: Audience models created following NAI guidelines for audience/contextual targeting for sensitive conditions
 - Keywords: Real-time keyword targeting based on keywords provided by agency, brand, or PulsePoint
 - Keyword Populations: Customer audiences that have recently engaged with content containing pre-specified keywords or health-specific keywords provided by PulsePoint
 - IBM Watson: Leverage real-world ZIP data where conditions are likely to be impacted by external factors (eg weather)
 
 We also have more generalized targeting capabilities such as retargeting, clickers, converters, IAB, demographic (age, gender, ethnicity), geography etc.
